summary: TLS half-close + HTTP/2 downgrade during streaming causes final attachment checksum to be dropped and interleaved system messages
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-form streaming responses which include attachments (base64 image footer + content-checksum metadata) occasionally arrive with the final attachment missing and with duplicated system messages interleaved near the end. The failure is correlated with an abrupt TLS half-close on the client path and a subsequent HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 downgrade at the edge.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: Final attachment (image footer and checksum) omitted from streaming response ~1-2% of long streams; downstream consumer rejects the response due to missing checksum.
- Workloads: Dedicated pool in us-west serving QuillDocs workspace.

Environment / context:
- Dedicated tenant, prod-us-west, edge-proxy chain includes corporate WAF -> CDN -> API gateway -> serving-runtime.
- Streaming method: SSE (fallback to long-lived HTTP/1.1 where upgrade fails) and WebSocket in an alternate path.
- Observed when model generates large multi-part payloads (attachments embedded as base64 and trailing metadata envelope).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Authenticate with QuillDocs dedicated API keys in us-west region.
2) Submit a long generation (approx 6-10k tokens) that includes an instruction to attach an image and a trailing checksum metadata envelope.
3) Simulate intermittent TLS half-close from client side (e.g., client closes TLS write channel) or force edge to downgrade to h1 by inserting a malformed ALPN on a path.
4) Observe SSE stream: in problematic runs the stream emits duplicated system messages and then terminates without the final attachment/checksum block.
logs: Customer-provided truncated SSE transcript attached to ticket (redacted): https://files.quilldocs.net/tmp/sse-trace-03-10.log
Edge access logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:07Z - client ip 54.204.x.x - TLS half-close observed - ALPN fallback to http/1.1
API gateway trace (trace id: 7c1d9e): worker reported connection reset during flush; serving-runtime returned 200 with missing trailer meta
Serving runtime logs: session 0x7f4a - streaming flush aborted after window update race; KV cache preserved; trailing envelope not serialized
comments: 2026-03-10 14:25 - quill-support@quilldocs.com: Customer: We've seen this 3 times in the last 24h, always for longer documents with images. Consumer pipeline fails validation because checksum is missing. Attached a client-side PCAP and SSE log.

2026-03-10 15:02 - Aisha Khan (Support): Thanks for the details — triaging and escalating to SRE/Runtime. Can you confirm if you saw a TLS-level close or an application close? You said 'half-close' in the PCAP notes.

2026-03-10 15:37 - SRE triage (Elena Park): Observed ALPN negotiation fallback on several traces. Edge reported upstream GOAWAY after TLS session renegotiate. Marking as P1 due to customer validation failures. Assigning to runtime on-call.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Miguel Ortega (Runtime Eng): Replicated locally with synthetic client that performs a TLS write-half-close during a streaming response behind an h2->h1 downgrade. Found race where trailer/envelope serialization is queued after stream write but connection shutdown path flushes earlier, causing attachment not to be sent.

2026-03-11 12:40 - Miguel Ortega (Runtime Eng): Hypothesis: on edge downgrade we re-enter a legacy HTTP/1.1 flush path that doesn't honor our async trailer buffer when a TLS half-close occurs from the client. Duplicated system messages appear when the control plane replays progress markers on reconnect.
investigation_notes: Observation 1: Failure frequency correlates with multi-hop path changes (CDN + WAF path) and TLS renegotiation attempts.
Observation 2: Serving runtime emits final JSON choice and marks stream complete, but the trailing attachment envelope is owned by a separate serializer that races with connection close.
Hypothesis: Connection-level half-close leads HTTP/2 stack to issue a stream reset vs a graceful end; the runtime's trailer writer has no retry when kernel-level flush fails on abrupt TLS closure.

Reproduction: Synthetic test using a proxy that intentionally performs TLS write-half-close during final trailer write reproduces missing trailer 9/10 runs if an ALPN fallback to h1 is forced; only 0/10 runs fail on pure h2 path.
Temporary mitigation attempted: pin route to h2-only upstream (via edge rule) for a subset of customer traffic — eliminated missing attachments in A/B tranche.
Related: see linked incident SUP-214159 (stream final segment omission during proxy rewrite) and SUP-420420 (edge-probe split fragment leading to orphaned tail).
resolution: Workaround applied + runtime fix in progress
resolution_notes: Workaround: Edge rule created to prefer HTTP/2 ALPN on QuillDocs tenant in prod-us-west (effective 2026-03-11T17:00Z). Mitigated customer-visible failures for the impacted production pool.

Fix in progress: Runtime change to make trailer/attachment serialization synchronous with final token flush when connection close is observed; added retry/flush path on TLS write errors. Engine PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1452 (WIP).

Follow-up actions:
- Create API gateway health-check to detect ALPN fallback spikes and surface as alert (operational task).
- Add unit/integration tests for TLS half-close + trailer flush race.
- Postmortem draft (linked confluence) to review long-term design: ensure trailing envelopes are part of main response path or persisted to ephemeral KV to retry on reconnect.
- Customer follow-up: schedule check-in with QuillDocs success manager once PR is deployed to staging and validated.
